diagnosis: EBV+ extramedullary plasmacytoma in an immunocompetent patient (EPIC)
legend: Biopsy of a fleshy exophytic lesion in the nasal cavity. The cellular infiltrate extends under intact, pre-existing normal epithelium (<<29259>>). The lesion is composed of mature and slightly enlarged plasma cells, with rare large bizarre cells and admixed small lymphocytes (<<29260>>). CD138 is diffusely positive (<<29261>>). Plasma cells also express monotypic IgA lambda (not shown). Neoplastic plasma cells are positive for EBV (in situ hybridization for EBV-encoded small RNA [EBER]) (<<29265>>).

diagnosis: Solitary plasmacytoma of bone with amyloid deposition
legend: A patient presented with pain and a lytic lesion in the femoral neck. The biopsy shows sheets of plasma cells and large aggregates of pale-pink amyloid (<<29894>>). At 25 months, a second lytic lesion was found, but the marrow remained negative. There is no known systemic amyloidosis. The lesion is composed of sheets of mature and slightly atypical plasma cells adjacent to amyloid with a fibrillar quality (<<29895>>). With Congo red stain, the amyloid is positive (<<29896>>), and apple-green in polarized light (<<29897>>).
